model_metadata:
### Source raw.raw_customers
Table: "ecommerce"."raw"."raw_customers"
Description: One row per customer account, extracted from the CRM.
Freshness: measured on `loaded_at`; warn after 1 hour, error after 2 hours
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description):
- customer_id · INTEGER · CRM primary key of the customer (integer).
- first_name · VARCHAR · Customer first name.
- last_name · VARCHAR · Customer last name.
- email · VARCHAR · Customer email address as entered in the CRM.
- country · VARCHAR · ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the customer's billing address.
- created_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the account was created in the CRM.
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the ingestion job wrote the row.
lineage:
DAG edges (upstream → downstream; tests omitted):
- source raw.raw_customers → model stg_customers
- model dim_customers → exposure finance_revenue_dashboard
- model dim_customers → exposure marketing_customer_dashboard
- model stg_customers → model dim_customers
Downstream nodes (affected if the failing node is wrong or skipped):
- model stg_customers (view): Cleaned customers, one row per customer. Email lower-cased, country code upper-cased.
- model dim_customers (table): One row per customer with order history and lifetime value. Used by marketing and finance dashboards.
- exposure finance_revenue_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Finance analytics): Daily revenue by payment method and order status. Refreshed at 07:00 UTC and used in the daily finance stand-up.
- exposure marketing_customer_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Marketing analytics): Customer counts, lifetime value and repeat-purchase rate by country.
Column-level lineage (as designed):
- stg_customers.customer_id ← raw_customers.customer_id
- stg_customers.{first_name, last_name, created_at, loaded_at} ← raw_customers (same names)
- stg_customers.email ← raw_customers.email (lower-cased)
- stg_customers.country_code ← raw_customers.country (upper-cased)
- dim_customers.{customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, country_code, created_at} ← stg_customers (same names)
- dim_customers.{first_order_date, most_recent_order_date, number_of_orders} ← stg_orders.order_date / order_id, per customer_id
- dim_customers.lifetime_value ← stg_payments.amount joined via stg_orders.order_id, non-cancelled orders, per customer_id

gold_standard_remediation.root_cause: Yesterday's DATA-140 commit changed raw_customers freshness in models/staging/sources.yml from warn 24 h / error 48 h to warn 1 h / error 2 h. Freshness is measured on max(loaded_at), and raw_customers only gets a row when a customer signs up, at most a couple a day. So max(loaded_at) is usually hours old even when the loader is healthy (now about 4 h). The CRM loader is working: the source is quiet, not stale.
gold_standard_remediation.fix: Revert the raw_customers freshness override in models/staging/sources.yml to `warn_after: {count: 24, period: hour}` and `error_after: {count: 48, period: hour}`. If hourly monitoring of the CRM loader is needed, check the loader's own run log or heartbeat instead of row timestamps.
gold_standard_remediation.verification: `dbt source freshness --select source:raw.raw_customers` passes, and its age falls within the historical range of 3–30 h.
gold_standard_remediation.text:
Root cause: Yesterday's DATA-140 commit changed raw_customers freshness in models/staging/sources.yml from warn 24 h / error 48 h to warn 1 h / error 2 h. Freshness is measured on max(loaded_at), and raw_customers only gets a row when a customer signs up, at most a couple a day. So max(loaded_at) is usually hours old even when the loader is healthy (now about 4 h). The CRM loader is working: the source is quiet, not stale.

Fix: Revert the raw_customers freshness override in models/staging/sources.yml to `warn_after: {count: 24, period: hour}` and `error_after: {count: 48, period: hour}`. If hourly monitoring of the CRM loader is needed, check the loader's own run log or heartbeat instead of row timestamps.

Verification: `dbt source freshness --select source:raw.raw_customers` passes, and its age falls within the historical range of 3–30 h.
